summary: South Korea admits citizens of over 100 countries without a visa for 30–180 days, normally subject to the K-ETA electronic travel authorization (10,000 KRW, valid 3 years) — though K-ETA has been temporarily waived for 22 countries including the US, UK and Japan; other nationalities apply for a C-3 short-term visit visa at an embassy.

fee.notes: About USD 7–8 according to the K-ETA portal, plus a 3% online card-payment charge, paid online by card; not refunded if the application is refused. Not a visa — an electronic travel authorization for visa-free nationals. Temporarily waived for 22 countries.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says that to enter South Korea as a tourist for up to 90 days, your passport must have an expiry date after the date you leave South Korea; for a long-term visa it should be valid at least 6 months after the date you arrive.

source.name: UK FCDO — South Korea entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for short-term visitors to South Korea. The UK Foreign Office says medical care is usually of a good standard but can be expensive, and advises adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds.

onwardTicket.text: The UK Foreign Office says visitors entering visa-free for up to 90 days must have an onward or return ticket.

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for South Korea.

declarations.text: Korea's free e-Arrival Card can be submitted online starting 3 days before arrival and holds the same validity as the paper arrival card. K-ETA holders are exempt from submitting an arrival card.

source.name: e-Arrival Card (Ministry of Justice) — e-Arrival Card Guide

currencyLimits.text: Currency and monetary instruments exceeding 10,000 USD in total (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Korea Customs Service — Declaration of foreign currency
source.instrument: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Article 17; Enforcement Decree, Article 31

notes: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to bring narcotic or psychotropic drugs into South Korea, even with a prescription, unless you have an import permit applied for online before you arrive.

The Korea Customs Service's duty-free allowance is goods worth up to USD 800 in total, plus, on top of that, alcohol of up to 2 litres and USD 400, 200 cigarettes, 20 ml of e-cigarette liquid nicotine and 100 ml of perfume; travellers under 19 get no allowance for alcohol or cigarettes.

The Korea Customs Service says meat, plants, fruit, vegetables and other agricultural, livestock and fishery products, including processed foods, must be declared on arrival. Goods over the allowance that are found undeclared carry an extra 40% on top of the duty.

payments.text: No official source we could read describes how widely cards are accepted in South Korea. Canada's travel advice says some major banks have ATMs that accept international debit or credit cards, though the amount per withdrawal may be low.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime against foreigners is rare but there are occasional thefts, and there have been cases of assault, including sexual assault, around bars and nightlife areas. South Korean authorities sometimes hold civil emergency exercises marked by sirens; the UK says to follow any instructions given.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season runs from late June to August, with July usually the wettest month, and that typhoons occur in August and September; the UK gives the typhoon season as June to November. The CIA World Factbook describes a temperate climate with heavier rain in summer and cold winters.

idp.text: South Korea is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for South Korea yet.

tips.text: The Ministry of Justice has extended the temporary K-ETA exemption to December 31, 2026 for the countries currently exempt. Apply only through the official K-ETA website, k-eta.go.kr (10,000 KRW); the UK Foreign Office says other sites offering K-ETA applications are generally scams.
Fill in the free e-Arrival Card online (e-arrivalcard.go.kr) within 3 days before arrival to skip the paper form at immigration.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa or K-ETA for South Korea?
faq.answer: US citizens do not need a visa for stays up to 90 days. A K-ETA is normally required, but it has been temporarily waived for US passport holders (along with 21 other countries), and the Ministry of Justice has extended the waiver to December 31, 2026.

faq.question: What is the K-ETA and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: The Korea Electronic Travel Authorization is an online pre-clearance for visa-free visitors, costing KRW 10,000 (about USD 7–8 according to the portal) plus a 3% online card-payment charge, and valid for 3 years for multiple visits. The portal says approval must be obtained before boarding and that assessment typically takes 72 hours or less. K-ETA holders also skip the arrival card at immigration.

faq.question: How long can Canadians stay in South Korea?
faq.answer: The K-ETA portal gives Canadian citizens an allowed stay of 6 months, the longest it lists. The K-ETA requirement is temporarily waived for Canadians, and the Ministry of Justice has extended the waiver to December 31, 2026.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit South Korea without a visa?
faq.answer: Individual Chinese travelers need a C-3 short-term visit visa. The Ministry of Justice announced a trial visa-free scheme for Chinese tour groups of 3 or more, recruited by designated agencies, for stays of up to 15 days, from 29 September 2025 to 30 June 2026; we have found no official notice extending it.

faq.question: How much does a South Korean tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that need one (including Indian, Filipino, Vietnamese and Indonesian citizens), the single-entry C-3 short-term visit visa costs USD 40 for stays up to 90 days; a double-entry visa costs USD 70 and an unlimited multiple-entry visa USD 90, as set by Article 71 of the Enforcement Rules of the Immigration Act. Missions collect the equivalent in local currency. Apply through a Korean embassy or designated visa center — see visa.go.kr.
